## seqeron 0.10.0

Clients can now snapshot their own state. Every instance of a participating application or gateway
serializes its state at a cut the log marks, into a local file the log confirms, and a restart restores
from the newest one instead of replaying from `globalSeqNo` 1 (`doc/snapshot.md`). Payloads may be up to
8884 bytes, and a cluster may have up to seven members.

The frame schema (`sbe-frame.xml`, 210) changed, so a 0.9.0 archive cannot be replayed by this release:
purge every node's archive and upgrade the whole deployment together (see Upgrading).

### Breaking changes

- **Schema 210 changed** (spec V-3). `GatewayRegistered` and `ApplicationRegistered` gained a `snapshot`
  field, `SnapshotStarted` (template 107), `SnapshotRequested`, `SnapshotEnd` and `SnapshotPolicyRegistered`
  are added, and the payload limit rose. Every member, gateway host, producer and consumer moves to 0.10.0
  at once, from purged archives.
- **`MAX_PAYLOAD_LENGTH` is 8884 bytes** (was 1316), and `MAX_INGRESS_LENGTH` 8912. A frame longer than its
  stream's MTU less 32 bytes is now fragmented, on the tap, its recording and a replay as on ingress. A
  consumer that reads a seqeron stream through its own subscription must reassemble, as Aeron's
  `FragmentAssembler` does; `ReplayerStreamReceiver` and the façades already do. Every stream that carries
  frames needs a term length of at least 128 KiB. C++ `ClusterStreamSender::MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN` is 16384.
- **`PortLayout.CLUSTER_MEMBER_COUNT` is now the maximum, 7** (C++ `protocol::CLUSTER_MEMBER_COUNT`). Code
  that used it for the default three-member cluster should use the new `DEFAULT_MEMBER_COUNT`, 3.
- **The reserved port block is 9300–9369** (was 9300–9329), so keep an application's own ports out of it.
  `SEQERON_PORT_BASE` must be at most 65466.
- **`ClusterError` has two new values**, `SNAPSHOT_DIVERGED` and `SNAPSHOT_UNRESTORABLE` (C++
  `SnapshotDiverged`, `SnapshotUnrestorable`). A switch over it needs both.
- **The IPC term length defaults to 16 MiB** on a member's and a gateway host's driver, rather than Aeron's
  64 MiB, which makes the tap's window 8 MiB. `-Daeron.ipc.term.buffer.length` sets another
  (`doc/ops.md`, "Term lengths").
- **A node's cluster layout comes from the host list alone.** `sequencer.nodeCount` and
  `sequencer.clusterMembers` are removed, and ignored if set: use `-Dsequencer.hosts` or `SEQERON_HOSTS`.
  With neither, a node is a one-member cluster on `localhost` and refuses a `sequencer.memberId` other than
  0. `ports.sh` loses `cluster_members_string`, `member_port`, `log_port` and `transfer_port`;
  `cluster_hosts_string` builds the host list instead.
- **Replay protocol (`sbe-replay.xml`, 212): a client replays one recording.** `ReplayRequest.segmentIndex`
  and `Replaying.recordingId` are removed. `fromPosition` = `ReplayProtocol.FROM_START` (−1, C++
  `protocol::REPLAYER_FROM_START`) asks for the active recording from its start; any other value resumes it
  there. In the spec, R-2 and R-3 are replaced by a single R-2, and R-4 and R-5 are now R-3 and R-4.
- **C++ `ClusterStreamClient` replays one recording.** `RecordingSegment`, `resolveClusterStreamSegments`
  and `start(aeron, archive, segments, replayChannel)` are removed. `start(aeron, archive, recordingId,
  catchUpPosition, replayChannel)` replays the recording `connectToArchiveWithClusterStream` or
  `connectLocalArchive` found from its start, and follows it live.
- **C++ `ReplayerStreamReceiver`'s constructor loses its last parameter**, the test-only
  `detail::TapFaultInjector`, which is removed.

### New

- **Application snapshots** (`doc/snapshot.md`):
  - The topology document's `<snapshots interval="…"/>` turns rounds on, and `snapshot="true"` on a
    gateway or application row makes that source take part. An interval of 0 means rounds start only on
    `clusterctl request-snapshot`, which is new.
  - A façade takes part through the builder's `snapshotListener` and `snapshotDirectory` (C++
    `Config::snapshotListener`, `Config::snapshotDirectory`). `SnapshotListener` encodes the state record by
    record in `onSnapshot`, restores it in `onRestore`, and names its format in `formatVersion`. Every
    instance writes its own file, the one that may publish submits the round's `SnapshotEnd`, and every
    instance checks its file against it.
  - A starting instance restores from its newest confirmed file and resumes after the cut.
    `ReplayerStreamReceiver` gains `restoreFrom`, `restart()` and `restoreFailure()` for a consumer that
    drives recovery itself.
  - `Gateway` instances may run passive (`passive(true)`, C++ `Config::passive`): no state until
    activated, then a restore and catch-up. `isPassive()` reports it.
  - Replay protocol (`sbe-replay.xml`, 212): `SnapshotQuery` (23) and `SnapshotLocation` (24), added in
    place. The `seqeron_replayer_snapshot_round` gauge shows each source's newest indexed round per node.
- **Up to seven members**, Raft's 3, 5 or 7, from the wider port block.
- **Larger payloads on an unfragmented tap.** `-Daeron.ipc.mtu.length=8960` keeps frames up to the new
  limit whole on the tap. A replay carries its recording's MTU, so every UDP replay of the tap then needs a
  9000-byte network MTU, for small frames too (`doc/ops.md`, "MTU"). At Aeron's default of 1408 nothing
  changes for payloads up to 1316 bytes.
- **`SbeLogPrinter` reassembles** fragmented frames, on the tap and in the Raft log.
- **A cold start replays the active recording only.** The cluster takes no snapshots, so every recording a
  node makes starts at `globalSeqNo` 1 and the active one holds the whole log: a stopped tap recording is no
  longer read, and may be deleted. The Replayer's startup check proves only the active recording. Its log
  lines changed to `ready — tap recording N live and verified from globalSeqNo 1; serving replay` and
  `replay for client C: recording R [from,tip) session S`.
- **Java `SequencedEvent` extends `SequencedFrameDecoder`**, which is no longer final, so an event has every
  accessor the decoder has. Only the receiver calls `wrap`.
- **Harnesses:** `snapshot-test.sh` drives a gateway pair and application replicas through restores,
  failovers and a passive activation; `paused-subscriber-test.sh` stops a tap subscriber under load. CI
  runs both. `ClusterProbe confirm` takes `probe.fillerBytes` (`CONFIRM_FILLER_BYTES` in
  `gateway-host-test.sh`).

### Fixed

- **A stopped tap subscriber no longer takes its member down.** Until its driver evicted it, an untethered
  subscriber that stopped polling (a GC pause, a debugger) held the tap's window, and a window's worth of
  traffic later the sequencer terminated with exit 70. A member's and a gateway host's driver now set
  `aeron.timer.interval` to 10 ms and the untethered window-limit and linger timeouts to 100 ms each (Aeron:
  1 s, 5 s, 5 s), so the subscriber is evicted within about 0.2 s and heals through replay
  (`doc/ops.md`, "Untethered subscribers").
- **`replay-bench.sh`** resolves the repository root, and runs again.
- **`gap-recovery-test.sh` and `chaos-runner.sh` detect a re-walk.** They counted a log line nothing emits,
  so their check that a gap was resumed rather than re-walked could never fail.

### Upgrading

- Stop every member and gateway host, purge their archive and cluster directories, and start 0.10.0 on all
  of them. Upgrade every producer and consumer at the same time.
- Run `clusterctl load-topology` again: a purged cluster has no list.
- To snapshot, add `<snapshots interval="…"/>` and `snapshot="true"` to the topology, and give each
  participating façade a `SnapshotListener` and a directory of its own that outlives the process.
- If you set `aeron.timer.interval` or the untethered timeouts yourself, keep both timeouts plus two timer
  intervals well inside 1 s.
- For payloads above 1316 bytes with jumbo frames, set `aeron.ipc.mtu.length=8960` identically on every
  member and gateway host, in one restart window.
- Replace `-Dsequencer.clusterMembers=…` and `-Dsequencer.nodeCount=…` with `-Dsequencer.hosts=…` or
  `SEQERON_HOSTS`. Nothing warns when the old properties are still set.
- Update monitoring that matches the Replayer's `ready` line, or a `replay for client … segment` line.
